title: Reliability partnerships workback and ops runbook (Q1 2025)
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a pragmatic workback plus lightweight runbook for the cross-functional reliability program deliverables tied to SLO adoption and operational readiness for Q1 2025. Aim: reduce ambiguity on handoffs, define the minimum acceptance criteria for services to be considered "reliability-ready", and create a repeatable weekly cadence for cross-team coordination.

Scope (what's in / out):
- In scope: platform services that carry customer latency/availability SLOs (hosted API, routing, KV cache, autoscaler), onboarding checklist for new models, and runbook templates for P0/P1 incidents.
- Out of scope: long-term infra refactors (multi-quarter infra rewrite), customer-facing SLAs amendments (legal owns), or billing changes.

Objectives (measurable):
1) 80% of high-traffic services have completed the "Service Reliability Readout" checklist by 2025-03-15.
2) Reduce median P1 mitigation time by 20% (baseline = Nov 2024) via clearer runbooks and dedicated play owners.
3) Establish a weekly cross-functional triage that resolves or routes 90% of outstanding reliability work items within 2 weeks.

Success metrics / guardrails:
- SLO coverage: percentage of customer-facing routes mapped to an SLO in the SLO registry.
- Runbook completeness score: checklist (pager escalation, mitigation steps, rollback, postmortem owner).
- Operational readiness: (oncall drills completed) / (oncall rotations) >= 0.9 per quarter.

Key stakeholders and roles:
- Eng SRE (Ava Chen): program lead, orchestrates weekly cadence, owns Runbook templates and readiness rubric.
- Platform engineering (Liam O'Connor): implementation owners for autoscaler, routing fallback.
- Serving runtime (Priya Nair): model KV cache, batching behavior, performance knobs.
- Product-hosted-api (Sofia Alvarez): product acceptance of fallbacks and rollouts.
- Solutions & Customer Success: validation for customer-impacting behaviors.
- Incident Commander pool: rotating list (see linked artifact PR).

High-level timeline (workback):
- Week 0 (2025-01-06): Program kickoff with stakeholders, agree on checklist and metrics.
- Week 1-2: Service owners complete self-assessments (SLO mapping + current runbook snapshot).
- Week 3-4: SRE reviews and provides remediation tickets (priority tag: reliability- remediation).
- Week 5-8: Implement fixes and small-runbook edits; perform one tabletop drill per critical service.
- Week 9-10: Final readouts and signoff; mark services as "reliability-ready" in registry.

Milestones & deliverables:
- Service Reliability Readout template (deliverable): filled by owner, reviewed by SRE.
- Central runbook repo: standardized YAML header for meta (owner, oncall, playbook link).
- Triage rhythm established: weekly 30m cross-functional sync + rotating deep-dive 60m per month.
- Tabletop drill reports: one per critical service.

Weekly rhythm (recommended):
- Monday: automated SLO health snapshot posted to #reliability-weekly (SRE automation).
- Wednesday: 30m cross-functional sync (blockers, new remediation tickets, escalations).
- Friday: Asynchronous status update in Confluence page + updated issue states.

Acceptance criteria for "reliability-ready" label:
- SLO defined and registered in SLO registry with target and measurement window.
- Runbook exists with: detection, immediate mitigation (<= 3 steps), escalation contact, rollback commands, and postmortem owner.
- Two successful tabletop drills (or one drill + one replay of a recent incident).
- Automated alerting configured and routed to oncall with reasonable noise thresholds.

Integration / test checklist (minimal):
- Canary traffic test for routing fallback (simulated 10% traffic shift).
- KV cache cold-start simulation: confirm latency within expected bounds.
- Autoscaler scale-up/down test under synthetic load.
- End-to-end smoke that validates model-variant fallback does not degrade integrity beyond accepted threshold.

Risk register (top items):
- Risk: Owners deprioritize remediation against feature work. Mitigation: SRE will attach small remediation tickets to ongoing sprints and flag in weekly sync.
- Risk: Runbook divergence (multiple doc formats). Mitigation: enforce template; any deviation flagged as "needs remediation" during readout.
- Risk: Alert fatigue from poorly tuned signals. Mitigation: pre-release alert review meeting and dynamic suppression window for new alerts.
- Risk: Cross-team communication gaps during urgent incidents. Mitigation: explicit escalation matrix + dedicated incident coordinator for 2-week window after rollout.

Communication plan (who says what to whom):
- Weekly sync notes: SRE -> cross-functional channel (#reliability-weekly).
- Major milestone (service marked ready): product + solutions notified, Confluence status updated, and ticket closed with release notes.
- Incident playbook changes: oncall -> repository PR -> two approvers (SRE + product) before merge.

Operational runbook snippets (placeholders to be expanded per service):
- Detection: alert "api-latency-p90 > 2000ms for 5m" triggers oncall page.
- First 3 actions: 1) Confirm alert via metrics dashboard and logs. 2) Shift traffic to canary/backup cluster (route: /v2 -> v1 fallback). 3) Clear KV cache warmers or switch to read-through cache if available.
- Escalation: If mitigation not effective in 15m, escalate to Eng SRE lead and trigger incident channel.

Open questions / items to resolve:
- Do we require two-tabletop drills for low-traffic but important services, or can we accept one drill + historical replay? (action: product to weigh risk appetite by 2025-01-13).
- Who is the final approver for adding a service to the "reliability-ready" list if the owner is unavailable? (proposal: SRE program lead plus product PM).
- How will Dedicated vs Hosted SLA differences be surfaced in the runbook? (action: platform engineering + product to draft mapping).

Next steps (this week):
- Ava: finalize Service Reliability Readout template and push to central repo by 2025-01-08.
- Service owners: complete self-assessment by 2025-01-15.
- SRE: create remediation ticket templates and automation to tag issues.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep readout short — 10m per service owner in the review.
- Prioritize services with both high traffic and >1 historical P1.
- Use the table-based spreadsheet for score tracking but source-of-truth remains the SLO registry.

Attachment references / helpful links: SLO registry, runbook repo, tabletop drill checklist in Confluence (see linked artifacts).

If you are a service owner and are unsure how to complete the self-assessment, ping me (Ava) or book 15m via the reliability office hours calendar.

-- end of doc --
